title: Prawn Jalfrezi
subtitle: A hot, dry-style curry of king prawns, peppers, and spiced tomato
excerpt: Prawns cook in minutes, so this jalfrezi comes together fast. The tomato-pepper base is punchy and slightly dry. The prawns go in last and need barely four minutes so they stay plump.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian restaurant tradition; jalfrezi with seafood is a popular British-Indian curry-house variation.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make the tomato-pepper base up to a day ahead. Add the raw prawns and cook through just before serving.

content.text: Prawn jalfrezi is a quick, high-heat curry where timing matters. The sauce cooks in about 15 minutes and the prawns go in at the very end. Overcooked prawns turn rubbery, so watch them closely once they are in the pan.
Heat the oil in a wide pan over high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 20 seconds. Add the onion and fry for 5 minutes until soft and lightly golden.
Add the garlic and ginger. Stir for one minute. Add the turmeric, coriander, and chilli powder. Stir for 30 seconds.
Add the tomato puree and tinned tomatoes. Cook for 8 minutes over medium heat, stirring often, until thick and the oil separates at the edges.
Add the sliced peppers. Stir over high heat for 3 minutes. They should soften at the edges but keep some bite.
Season the base with salt. Add the raw prawns and stir to coat in the sauce.
Cook over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until every prawn has turned pink and opaque. Do not cook longer.
Stir in the garam masala and scatter over fresh coriander. Serve immediately with rice or flatbreads.

items.symptom: The prawns are rubbery and tough.
items.cause: They cooked too long in the hot sauce.
items.fix: Add prawns only when the base is fully cooked and remove the pan from the heat the moment every prawn is pink. Carryover heat finishes them.

items.symptom: The sauce is watery and does not cling to the prawns.
items.cause: The tomato base was not reduced before the peppers went in.
items.fix: Cook the tomato sauce until it is thick and jammy, with oil pooling at the sides, before adding anything else.

items.cause: The spices were not fried long enough in the onion base.
items.fix: Give the ground spices a full 30 seconds in the dry pan before the tomatoes go in. A squeeze of lemon juice at the end lifts the whole dish.
